architecture.summary: A Node server that serves Prelude’s pages, runs the agent one turn per design, and serves each design on an origin of its own, as that app’s server would. The desktop app is a window on it. Everything it produces is a file in the project’s folder.

principles.title: The folder is the database.
principles.why: Everything Prelude produces is a file under prelude/, committed with the code. ~/.prelude holds only this machine’s conveniences, so nothing is lost if it goes.

principles.title: The server is the one source of live state.
principles.why: Every window, the pop-out and a browser tab render from the server and follow it over its live channel, so none holds what another needs.

principles.title: Code the agent wrote runs only in the sandbox.
principles.why: A design’s views are JavaScript written by the agent; rendering them in the server would undo the fences on what the agent may read and write.

principles.title: Prelude knows no stack.
principles.why: A host renders the views; Prelude does everything else (routes, states, forms, the check), so every stack gets all of it.

principles.title: Committed files merge cleanly.
principles.why: Several people work on one project on different branches: names never collide, transcripts only grow, and no index is rewritten by every session.

principles.title: A design’s memory is its files.
principles.why: A design spans many sessions; each starts from the design’s files and notes, never from an earlier conversation.

principles.title: Every native feature has a web fallback.
principles.why: The desktop app makes things nicer. It never makes them possible.

decisions.title: The code is checked against each part’s declared uses
decisions.context: An architecture that isn’t checked drifts from the code within weeks, and an agent reading it is then misled.
decisions.decision: After every turn that changes code, Prelude reads the imports of the files that changed, finds each file’s part, and lists any use a part doesn’t declare, any file no part names, and any named file that isn’t there.
decisions.consequences: Build and fix agents are told the findings with their next message, as render failures are. Each finding is fixed in the code, or the architecture is changed by a proposed decision. JavaScript imports first; other stacks later.

decisions.title: Prelude reads a project’s architecture from its files
decisions.context: The architecture is written for agents as markdown files. A gallery of views over states would say everything twice.
decisions.decision: Prelude reads architecture/ (overview, parts, decisions, flows) as it reads RULES.md, and shows it on the project’s Architecture pages.
decisions.consequences: The files are the one source; the pages can’t drift from them. The architecture design has no states of its own.

decisions.title: A fix is its own kind of work, on its own branch
decisions.context: Some problems belong to no one design: a page that breaks only when clicked into, a layout the app never got.
decisions.decision: A fix is one problem, in prelude/fixes/<slug>/, worked on in sessions on the branch prelude/fix-<slug>. Its agent may change the app and every design.
decisions.consequences: A fifth noun in the model. A fix that changes a built page changes its design too, so the designs stay the specification.

decisions.title: One layout for all the app’s pages

supersedes.title: A workspace layout for a design’s page

decisions.context: A design’s page clicked into from Home arrived without the workspace layout’s stylesheet, so nothing filled the window.
decisions.decision: A design’s page is in the app layout, links its own stylesheet and marks its root .fills. Only a genuinely different document (the pop-out) has a layout of its own.
decisions.consequences: Moving between pages never reloads the document. A page that fills the window says so in its own markup.

decisions.title: A workspace layout for a design’s page

supersededBy.title: One layout for all the app’s pages

decisions.context: The design page fills the window while other pages scroll.
decisions.decision: The design page renders in its own workspace layout.
decisions.consequences: Moving between layouts needs a whole page; Koda swaps only the main region.

decisions.title: Every design works on its own branch, in a worktree
decisions.context: A design and its build change the same files as other designs, and the person’s checkout is theirs.
decisions.decision: Each design works on prelude/<design> in a worktree of its own. Every turn is committed there; Prelude never writes to the checkout.
decisions.consequences: A worktree is a project of its own to the server, with its own sessions, host and check. Finishing merges or pushes for a pull request.

decisions.title: Other stacks render through a host spoken to over HTTP
decisions.context: Only one piece of serving a design knows Eta: rendering a view with its data.
decisions.decision: A project whose app isn’t Eta names a host in prelude/prelude.json. It renders over HTTP; Prelude does everything else.
decisions.consequences: Every stack gets routes, states, overlays, forms and the check. A host runs unsandboxed, so it starts only once approved.

decisions.title: Posts change a working copy, never the state’s file
decisions.context: A design that can’t save isn’t a prototype, but its states are the agent’s, and its fixtures.
decisions.decision: A post changes an in-memory copy of the current state, which every route reads. Picking a state, or Reset data, throws it away.
decisions.consequences: Restarting Prelude resets every copy. The state files stay the design’s truth.

decisions.title: Each design is served on an origin of its own
decisions.context: A design’s routes should be the app’s real URLs, root-relative, with ko-scope="/" owning the page.
decisions.decision: Each design is served at <design>.<project>.preview.localhost, with Koda, the system and the shell under /_prelude/.
decisions.consequences: Views port to the app unchanged. Posts to Prelude itself are refused from those origins.

decisions.title: A design is the app’s views, a route table and design-wide states
decisions.context: A screen flattened into one file drifts from the app at the first port.
decisions.decision: A design is the app’s views decomposed as the app decomposes them, a routes.json, and states that are one dataset each, read by every route.
decisions.consequences: The list, the detail and every fragment agree. After porting, the states are the view’s fixtures.

decisions.title: Views render in a sandboxed process
decisions.context: Eta templates are JavaScript, and a design’s views are written by the agent.
decisions.decision: Views render in a separate Node process under the permission model: it may read the project and Prelude, and nothing else.
decisions.consequences: Rendering costs a process hop. Node’s permission model doesn’t cover the network yet.

decisions.title: The desktop app starts the server when none answers
decisions.context: Starting the server by hand before opening the app was a step nobody wanted.
decisions.decision: The app uses a server already answering on localhost:4200, or starts node start.js itself and stops it on quit.
decisions.consequences: The server stops by itself if the app dies. A server the app didn’t start is left running.

decisions.title: The agent uses ordinary file tools, not domain tools
decisions.context: Everything a design is, is a file the agent can read.
decisions.decision: The agent reads and writes with Read, Write, Edit, Glob and Grep, fenced by path. There are no tools of Prelude’s own.
decisions.consequences: With no shell, it deletes a file by emptying it, and Prelude removes it when the turn ends.

flows.title: A turn
flows.summary: From the person’s message to the check that follows the agent’s answer.

steps.text: The message is posted from the composer, from Prelude’s own origin.
If the design has a turn running, the message waits; otherwise this turn starts.
Runs the Claude CLI in the design’s worktree, with the kind’s prompt, the findings from the last check, and its permissions.
Each streamed event goes to the session’s windows as it’s written.
Finished messages are appended to the transcript.
When the turn ends, the files it emptied are deleted and the turn is committed.
Renders every route in every state, and compares the pages with the approved screens.
Pages that don’t render are kept for the agent’s next message; the next waiting message starts.

decisions.title: Every design works on its own branch, in a worktree
The agent uses ordinary file tools, not domain tools

flows.title: A deep link to a drawer
flows.summary: A cold load of an overlay’s URL on a design’s origin: the page beneath, with the drawer open.

steps.text: A request to a design’s origin is handed to the design host.
Matches the overlay’s route, and its over page, filling the same :params.
Both routes’ data are found in the working copy, or the current state’s file.
Renders the page, the overlay and the layout in one job; the layout prints the drawer from its regions.
Answers the whole page, marked as Koda’s, with each region’s location set.

flows.title: A form posted in a design
flows.summary: A save in a design’s drawer: refused, or changing the working copy and answering the regions.

steps.text: Matches the POST route, and checks its required fields.
If one is empty, re-renders the form with what was typed and the messages, answered with a 422.
Otherwise updates, adds or removes at the data path, on a copy that becomes the working copy.
Renders the answer from the changed data, and each region it refreshes or closes.
Answers the fragment and its envelopes; nothing is announced, so the page keeps its place.
